subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: IronBridge POC — environment checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Devon Liu <devon.liu@ironbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: IronBridge POC — environment checklist & next steps

Hi Devon —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a concise checklist for the POC environment. Below are the core items we need to close to start your trial workload on Redwood Dedicated: 

- Org and tenant setup: create IronBridge org (contact: devops@ironbridge.ai) and provide the tenant ID so we can seed service accounts.
- API keys: we will create a short-lived demo API key for sandbox testing and hand over rotation guidance.
- IP allowlist: please confirm the egress IP ranges for IronBridge test VMs (see table in attachment).
- VPC peering: request a peering window (preferred: 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-14). We will coordinate firewall rules and route exchanges.

Deliverables attached:
- ironbridge_map_v1.pdf (MAP with milestones and owners)
- rbw-network-diagram-20260603.png (network topology for peering)
- rbw-temp-api-key-stub.txt (placeholder — we will not send keys over email; see secure transfer note in MAP)

As next steps, can you confirm:
1) Tenant ID and primary contact for org setup by EOD Friday (2026-06-04).
2) A preferred maintenance window for VPC peering (we suggested 6/10-6/14).
3) Any internal compliance requirements for ephemeral keys (rotation cadence, KMS references).

If those three items are green, we’ll schedule a 30-minute technical handoff with your network team and our infra engineer (Ben).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

From: Devon Liu <devon.liu@ironbridge.ai>

Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: IronBridge POC — environment checklist & next steps

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the MAP and attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- API keys: Our security team insists on HSM-backed keys for any long-running demos. For short sandbox keys, will Redwood provide a key with an explicit TTL and rotation policy? We prefer <24h demo keys for initial tests.
- IP allowlist: We can provide our test egress IPs but need to confirm if Redwood requires a /24, /22, or single IP entries per endpoint.
- VPC peering: 6/10–6/14 looks doable; our network ops prefer doing peering on 6/11 evening (after 22:00 UTC) to avoid weekday load. Please confirm Redwood's availability for that slot.

Cc’ing Asha (network lead) to share the tentative egress IP block: 54.210.72.0/24 and 18.204.5.128/25. Asha — we expect to finalize once Redwood confirms required ranges.

Thanks,
Devon
Director of Product | IronBridge AI
devon.liu@ironbridge.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Devon Liu <devon.liu@ironbridge.ai>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@ironbridge.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 18:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: IronBridge POC — environment checklist & next steps

Devon / Asha —

Appreciate the quick reply. A few technical points to make scheduling easier (copying the relevant parts of the MAP):

1) API keys and TTLs
- We can generate demo keys with a configurable TTL. For the sandbox, 12–24 hour TTLs are standard and acceptable. For anything longer we recommend using KMS and rotating keys daily.
- We will not send secrets via email. After tenant creation we will provision a short-lived key and share it through our secure key transfer (DocuSign/secret sharing link included in MAP).

2) IP allowlist granularity
- Single IP entries are supported, but to reduce management overhead we prefer CIDR entries where possible. For our hosted endpoints we advertise the following egress ranges that you can allow: 34.72.128.0/23, 34.72.130.0/24 (these are the endpoints used by the Dedicated sandbox for the trial). If you must restrict to a single address for a particular test VM, identify that VM and we’ll provide a temporary narrow-range mapping.

3) VPC peering steps & timing
- We can accept the 2026-06-11 22:00 UTC window. Proposed sequence (30–45m):
  a) Pre-flight check (10m): route tables, CIDR overlap, firewall state.
  b) Create peering and accept (10m).
  c) Route propagation and smoke tests (10–20m).
- Required info from you before peering: IronBridge VPC ID, primary CIDR, and the peering contact (network engineer with console access).

Action items for IronBridge to return: Tenant ID, confirmation of 6/11 22:00 UTC, and whether you want CIDR-level or single-IP allowlist for initial tests.

I’ll prepare a short network-runbook (attachment: rbw-network-runbook-peering-steps.md) and a signed MAP update after we get tenant ID.

Ben Carter
Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: rbw-network-runbook-peering-steps.md (md)

Thanks everyone — quick confirmation and proposed timeline: 

MAP status (short):
- Tenant ID: pending (Devon to share by EOD 2026-06-04)
- API key: Redwood will provision a 12h TTL demo key after tenant creation; production keys use KMS and daily rotation (Ben to assist).
- IP allowlist: IronBridge provided two CIDRs (54.210.72.0/24, 18.204.5.128/25). Redwood will temporarily accept those and also allow 34.72.128.0/23 and 34.72.130.0/24 on our side.
- VPC peering window: confirmed for 2026-06-11 22:00 UTC. Ben will run the network-runbook and coordinate the accept step.

Scheduled calls:
- Technical handoff (30m) — 2026-06-07 15:00 UTC (Ben + Asha + IronBridge devops). Calendar invite will follow.
- Peering execution (45m) — 2026-06-11 22:00 UTC (network ops).

Next immediate asks for IronBridge: Tenant ID + primary network contact (console access) + approval to accept our sandbox CIDRs. Please reply in-thread with that info. We’ll then attach an updated MAP with milestone dates and a DocuSign secure key transfer link.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
